items.title: 67425_Tiny Grimes oral history interview
items.q: I had to ask another fella's mother could he go out, Ray Bryant, but I heard him play

ctx.x: Cleveland Ohio. I went there for two weeks, stayed 2 years. And I discovered quite a few fellas, you know... Sonny Payne, I had to ask his mother, could he come out on the road, after I found out he could play. And his father was in

Chis Columbo down in Atlantic City. And they let him go out. I had to ask another fella's mother could he go out, Ray Bryant, but I heard him play, and said this cat sure could play -- young kid, you know, he couldn't go, so I had to ask his mother could he go. She ok'd it. Red Prysock had just got out of the army or navy or somethin', and... But those are some of the fellas that I helped get started in a way of speakin'. Screamin' Jay Hawkins had just got out of the airforce, I believe -- or navy or somethin'.…
Did you make any records with him?

items.title: Ray Bryant interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: He gained valuable experience in his home town with guitarist Tiny Grimes

ctx.x: Pianist Ray Bryant was born to a musical family in Philadelphia on December 24, 1931. He gained valuable experience in his home town with guitarist Tiny Grimes and as house pianist at the Blue Note. Ray moved to New York in the late 50s and performed and recorded with Carmen McRae, Sonny Rollins, Jo Jones and numerous other jazz luminaries. “Little Susie” and “Cubano Chant”

are among Ray’s original tunes which became popular on his own trio recordings. He tours abroad frequently and enjoys a special status in Japan with fellow pianist Junior Mance. His most recent recording is “Ray’s Tribute to his Jazz Piano Friends.”
